figures.finding: The National Film and Video Foundation grants up to R2.2 million (post-production included) to produce a fiction feature for experienced (tier 1) and less experienced (tier 2) filmmakers, up to R260,000 to develop one, and releases production money only once 75% of the finance is confirmed from other sources; its production and development grants are recouped from the film's gross profit alongside the producer.

tiers.1: at least three successful and commercially viable features, series, TV films or documentaries
tiers.2: one or two features, TV films or documentaries, or at least two shorts or commercials
tiers.3: new entrants who have produced or directed at least one short

value.recoupment: recoupable from gross profit, pari passu with the producer by default; not for shorts

figures.applies: South Africa; NFVF development and production grants to South African production companies; policy dated April 2026, published September 2026, read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: NATIONAL FILM AND VIDEO FOUNDATION FUNDING POLICY APRIL 2026 … 15. PRODUCTION 15.1. FICTION … Feature film (fiction) inclusive of post-production R 2 200 000.00 1 and 2 Made-for-TV movies R 350 000.00 1, 2, and 3 … For fiction projects (live action and animation), confirmation of a minimum of 75% derived from other funding categories will be required to enable the signing of contracts and release of payments by the NFVF.

figures.finding: The dtic's South African Film and Television Production Incentive refunds 35% of qualifying South African production expenditure, plus 5% more for productions with at least 30% Black South African heads of department and 30% of spend from Black-owned suppliers, up to R25 million a project; a production needs at least R1.5 million of qualifying spend (R500,000 for documentaries), 75% of its budget spent in South Africa, 60% of principal photography there, a South African director, and 25% of its finance committed when it applies.

value.status: under review from August 2026; applications already received processed under existing guidelines; adjudication resumed 2026-08-27; R727.8m and R503.5m in claims paid in 2024/25 and 2025/26; about R255m outstanding at 2026-06-30

figures.applies: South Africa; South African production companies with a special purpose vehicle and B-BBEE level 3 (SPCV level 4); feature films, TV and documentaries; guidelines issued September 2023, programme under review from August 2026.

sources.said: Incentive is calculated at thirty-five percent (35%) of Qualifying South African Production Expenditure (QSAPE). … The incentive programme offers a reimbursable grant to the maximum of R25 million per qualifying project.

As at 30 June 2026, the programme's outstanding liability amounted to approximately R255 million.

figures.finding: Under the dtic incentive, South African producer fees (at most two working producers) count toward the rebate only up to the lesser of 10% of total production expenditure or R1 million, company overheads up to the lesser of 2% or R200,000, and executive producer fees are financing costs that do not count.
figures.applies: South Africa; what counts as qualifying expenditure under the dtic South African Film and Television Production Incentive (guidelines issued September 2023); a cap on what the rebate pays on, not on what a producer may be paid.

sources.said: Producer fees South African producer fees, limited to two working producers and inclusive of all their travel accommodation and living expenses, are excluded from QSAPE to the extent that they exceed the lesser of: o 10% of the total of the company’s TPE on the film production; or o R1 million in total.

figures.finding: Of 253 films released in South African cinemas in 2023, the NFVF counts 8 domestic films (7 in its origin breakdown), down from 11 in 2022, and they took R5.2 million, 0.9% of the R575.0 million box office.
figures.applies: South Africa, theatrical releases January to December 2023 (NFVF report published 2025); the report gives both 8 and 7 for the domestic count.

sources.said: Of the 253 titles released at the box office, 8 were domestic films, a decline of 27.27% compared to 11 titles released in 2022. … These domestic films contributed only 0.9% (RSA GBO = R5.2 million) to the total revenue of R575.0 million.

figures.finding: The Independent Producers Organisation represents South Africa's independent film, television and digital producers; its executive committee approves each application, and annual fees run from R500 for an individual to R1,000 to R20,000 for a production company by turnover.

figures.applies: South Africa; independent producers and production companies; page dated 14 August 2023, updated 6 November 2024, read 2026-11-01.

The Independent Producers Organisation (IPO) represents, protects, and promotes the interests of independent South African film, television, and digital media producers

figures.finding: The NFVF's sixth Presidential Employment Stimulus round (PESP6) drew 1,787 applications (1,427 compliant) and approved 273: 110 production projects (R65.0 million), 74 training and 84 marketing projects, and five 'Blockbuster' features and documentaries chosen from 179 applications (113 compliant) that asked for R1.07 billion against a R50 million budget.
figures.applies: South Africa, NFVF-administered Presidential Employment Stimulus Programme, sixth round, approvals announced August and September 2026; the NFVF's regular funding cycles are counted separately.

sources.said: The NFVF has approved funding for 268 projects, representing a total investment of R150,493,669.00 … Stream 1: Production (Group 2) – Project 1 110 projects R64,977,833.97 in approved funding … Stream 2: Skills Development and Training 74 projects … Stream 3: Marketing and Distribution – Project 1 84 projects … PESP6 attracted 1,787 applications , of which 1,427 were compliant across the Blockbuster category and Streams 1, 2 and 3.

Five projects have been approved for funding … The Blockbuster group, aimed at supporting tier-one filmmakers and projects, attracted 179 applications , of which 113 were compliant . The compliant applications requested a combined R1.07 billion , against an allocated budget of R50 million
